calls.headline: IMF staff deal on the final review unlocks up to $2.3bn
calls.body: The IMF and Egypt reached a staff-level agreement on the eighth and final review of the loan program, which could release up to $2.3bn once the IMF board approves it, before the program expires on December 15 (EnterpriseAM, The National, Zawya). The central bank's dollar rate held at EGP 53.75 to buy and 53.89 to sell on Thursday morning, within 1% of its strongest in a year. The economy grew 4.9% year on year in July to September, the Planning Ministry told the Cabinet (Daily News Egypt, Arab Finance).
calls.view: The deal removes the main local risk to the pound before the Fed's December 9 decision: it keeps foreign money in T-bills even as 5% US yields shrink the carry. The desk expects the pound to stay firmer than EGP 55 into the central bank's December 17 meeting, which helps banks with large T-bill books, CIB first. Medium confidence: a bigger Fed hike than the quarter point priced would test it.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 17.

calls.headline: EGX30 slips 0.26% on its thinnest turnover in a year
calls.line: Turnover fell to EGP 6.7bn, about 40% below the 90-day average, as 119 stocks fell and 78 rose.
calls.body: The EGX30 fell 0.26% to 51,544.80 on Wednesday and the EGX70 EWI 0.16% to 17,564.30 (Masrawy, Al Mal). Turnover dropped to EGP 6.7bn, its lowest in at least a year and about 40% below the 90-day average (Al Mal); 119 stocks fell, 78 rose and 25 were unchanged (Arab Finance). Egyptians made 87.8% of trading, foreigners 9.3% and Arabs 2.9% (Arab Finance). The reports of net flows disagree, so the desk does not say who sold.
calls.view: A market waiting, not selling: there is little local news to sell on, but buyers are holding back until the IMF board vote and MSCI's November 30 changes. The desk expects the EGX30 to hold above 50,000 into them. Low confidence: thin markets move on little.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 49,500 before November 30.

calls.headline: EFG Holding jumps 5% as its investment bank carries the quarter
calls.line: Profit fell 15% to EGP 720m, but EFG Hermes' revenue rose 36%.
calls.body: EFG Holding rose 5.0% to EGP 25.30 on about six times Tuesday's volume. Third-quarter revenue rose 5% to EGP 6.7bn and profit after tax and minorities fell 15% to EGP 720m; excluding last year's one-off income and a non-recurring Bank NXT staff expense it rose 96% to EGP 805m. EFG Hermes' revenue rose 36% to EGP 2.9bn and EFG Finance's 26% to EGP 1.9bn, while Bank NXT's fell 31% to EGP 1.8bn (Khaleej Times, EnterpriseAM, Daily News Egypt).
calls.view: The market looked through the headline fall to a recovering investment bank, which earns more as turnover and listings pick up after the IMF deal. The desk expects the shares to hold most of the gain, at low confidence: Bank NXT is still shrinking and turnover is at a one-year low.
calls.wrong: EFG Holding closes below EGP 23 before December 31.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction doubles quarterly profit on US data centers
calls.line: Its backlog reached a record $11.6bn a week before 97.2 million new shares list.
calls.body: Orascom Construction's third-quarter profit attributable to shareholders rose 103% to $102.7m on revenue up 22.5% to $1.8bn, and US data-center work lifted its backlog to a record $11.6bn, excluding BESIX (EnterpriseAM, AGBI). The shares rose 0.8% to EGP 822.02. Its new shares for the OCI merger list on the EGX and in Abu Dhabi on November 24.
calls.view: Earnings now rest on US data centers as much as Egypt and the Gulf, which the EGX price does not fully reflect. The listing adds supply, but the desk expects the backlog to keep the shares near their highs. Medium confidence: new shares can weigh for a few sessions.
calls.wrong: Orascom Construction closes below EGP 740 before December 31.

calls.headline: Gulf strikes spread, but a US crude build pushes Brent to $91.95
calls.line: Cheaper oil trims Egypt's fuel bill, while Houthi fire on Riyadh puts the Red Sea back at risk.
calls.body: Brent settled 1.28% lower at $91.95 on Wednesday and WTI 3.2% lower at $83.26, after US crude stocks rose 3.4m barrels against about 58,000 expected (MLQ.ai citing Reuters, Invezz). The Houthis fired missiles at Riyadh on Wednesday night; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted them (Daily News Egypt, via AFP). Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit mines east of Hormuz, which has not been independently confirmed.
calls.view: For Egypt the oil price is the bigger channel: Brent is down about 22% since October 30, cutting the fuel and LNG import bill. Renewed Houthi fire is a risk to the Suez recovery, not yet to the oil price. The desk expects Brent to stay below $105, at medium confidence.

calls.headline: Anthropic prices at $83, raising a record $81.3bn
calls.body: Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83, above its $70–78 range, raising about $81.3bn before fees at a valuation near $1.5tn, the largest listing on record (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, TradingView). It starts trading on the Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday, probably after 5pm Cairo. Amazon, which will hold 14.7% after the listing according to the filing (Times of India), rose 3.82% to $267.74 on Wednesday, and Nasdaq 100 futures were up more than 1% on Thursday morning.
calls.view: Demand above the range shows investors still pay up for the companies building AI models, even as they sell the software those models could replace. The desk expects Amazon to keep its gain into November 27, at low confidence: a weak first trade would reverse it quickly.

calls.headline: Medicare audit plan sinks Humana 13% and UnitedHealth 10%
calls.line: Health insurers led the S&P 500's fifth straight fall, its longest since June.
calls.body: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services proposed tighter anti-fraud audits and oversight of Medicare and Medicaid plans, raising fears of payments being clawed back. Humana fell 12.98% to $385.78, UnitedHealth 10.2% and Elevance 7.6% (Benzinga via TradingView, Seeking Alpha, Beinsure). The S&P 500 lost 0.23% to 7,323.63 and the Dow 1.11%, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42%.
calls.view: A proposed rule with a comment period ahead leaves the size of the hit unknown, and uncertainty is what the sector is being priced for. The desk expects managed care to stay under pressure into the year-end, at low confidence: the rule can be softened.

calls.headline: Palo Alto's 39% revenue rise and $4.5bn deal lift cyber stocks
calls.line: Okta rose 12.1%, SailPoint 10.3% and Rubrik 9.3% with Palo Alto's 9.9%.
calls.body: Palo Alto Networks' quarterly revenue rose 39% to $3.44bn, with adjusted earnings of $1.05 a share, and it agreed to buy Applied Compute for $4.5bn in stock (Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, CTech). Its shares rose 9.9%, and investors bought the group: Okta rose 12.1% to $195.61 (Yahoo Finance); Rubrik also had new Microsoft products and a higher Cantor Fitzgerald target (MarketBeat).
calls.view: AI raises the threat and the budget: security is the part of software that gains from AI rather than being replaced by it. The desk expects cyber stocks to outperform the rest of software into the year-end, at low confidence after a one-day jump of this size.

calls.headline: Fed minutes back a December hike as the dollar hits a 19-month high
calls.line: Futures put about 95% odds on a quarter-point rise on December 9.
calls.body: Minutes of the Fed's October 27–28 meeting showed some officials favored a rate increase then, and a couple floated more than a quarter point in December. Futures put about 95% odds on a quarter-point rise on December 9 (247 Wall St.), the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.07% and the dollar index rose to 103.81, its highest since April 2025. Gold fell 3.2% to $3,741.90.
calls.view: Rates go up, not down, through the year-end, and a half point is now a real risk. That weighs on gold, long-duration tech and emerging-market carry. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The 10-year Treasury yield closes below 4.75% before December 9.

view.headline: The IMF deal keeps the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: The staff deal on the final review, worth up to $2.3bn, removes the main local risk before the program expires on December 15, and growth of 4.9% in July to September supports the case. With the one-year bill at 26.07%, record remittances and Brent down about 22% since October 30, the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55. The risks are US 10-year yields above 5%, a half-point Fed hike and a delay at the IMF board.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a debt auction clears with bids below the amount offered.
